title: Understanding the People Behind the Fight
gist: A Marine Pulse episode note: retired Marine intelligence officer Ben Connable discusses his critique of the Human Terrain System, how the Marine Corps can maintain cultural knowledge and adapt intelligence practices, and his RAND and Battle Research Group work on assessing units' will to fight.

themes.theme: Cultural intelligence and will to fight

insights.claim: Ben Connable, now at RAND and the Battle Research Group, focuses research on assessing a military unit's will to fight and learning from battlefield experience, drawing on advisory duty in Iraq and attaché duty in Jordan.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Will-to-fight assessment is an input to judging conflict duration and outcomes; a qualitative factor in geopolitical risk models.

insights.claim: The episode revisits Connable's critique of the Human Terrain System and examines how the Marine Corps can preserve cultural knowledge and adapt its intelligence practices.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Low direct market relevance; a signal of doctrine debates on human-centric intelligence.
